column1: # Where each Italian noun's gender in lex-it.tsv was read.
# The tooltip prints a noun's gender beside it, under both forms a row
# weaves. On 2026-10-08 every Italian noun was read against English
# Wiktionary's Italian entry, fetched raw: 177 of the 178 rows carry the
# gender of their page's Italian noun, and insegnante, teacher, masculine
# or feminine by the person meant, carries one of the two, as the Old
# English and French ledgers have it.
# The same reading found five wrong earlier that night, and they are right
# now: orecchio, ear, was neuter, a gender Italian does not have, and osso,
# braccio, dito and uovo were woven in their feminine plurals, ossa,
# braccia, dita and uova, under the masculine their singulars print. All
# five are masculine and woven in the singular only; see the header of
# lex-it.tsv. Every plural the seed weaves was then read against the
# plural forms its entry marks with a gender, and none now differs from
# tests/tools/genders.test.ts requires every noun in lex-it.tsv to have a
# line here giving the gender the seed gives, citing the noun's own entry,
# and fails on a line outliving its noun.
# ---- drafted from English Wiktionary via kaikki.org (dump of 2026-11-09), decided_by=wiktionary, status=proposed: woven, labelled, not yet read by a person ----
